rows.q: Do I need a receipt for a $30 expense if I work from the US?
rows.answer: No. US team members only need to submit receipts for expenses over $50 USD, so a $30 expense does not require a receipt. [1][2]

rows.q: I've left the company but still have an unpaid expense. How do I get reimbursed?
rows.answer:
1. Verify the expense has not already been processed in Navan. [1]  
2. Submit the valid receipts and a completed Expense Reimbursement template to Accounts Payable, including your manager’s approval. [1]  
3. Provide any required banking details so the payment can be sent to you. [1]  
4. Accounts Payable will aim to process and pay the reimbursement within one week. [1]
cited: Global Travel and Expense Policy > 7. OTHER > Expense Reimbursement for Terminated Team Members

rows.q: How long does it take to get my expense reimbursement paid out?
rows.answer:
- If you are a Team Member under a US expense policy, the reimbursement is processed through Navan **within 1–4 business days after the report is “final approved.”** [2]  
- For Team Members in non‑US GitLab entities that are paid through their payroll provider or GitLab AP, the report must be “final approved” **by EOD Tuesday** to be paid in that week; reports approved Wednesday‑Friday are paid the following week. Payments are made in the normal weekly payroll run and will appear in NetSuite once the AP payment is created. [2]  
- For many legal entities (e.g., GitLab Inc, GitLab Ltd (UK), GitLab BV, etc.), Navan batches approved expenses into a **single weekly payment paid on Monday**, which is deposited in the team member’s bank account **on Tuesday or Wednesday** (covering all expenses approved up to Sunday evening). [3]  
- Contractors reimbursed via iiPay receive payment **by the 22nd of each month** if expenses are submitted and approved by the 3rd. [4]  

Thus, payout timing depends on your legal status and entity: US 1‑4 business days; non‑US payroll by the weekly run (Tuesday/Wednesday for Navan batches); iiPay contractors by the 22nd of the month.
cited: Accounting and Reporting > Expenses > Team Member Reimbursements - Navan > Paying Navan Reports
Global Travel and Expense Policy > Approved Office Supplies List > Legal entities
Global Travel and Expense Policy > Approved Office Supplies List > Legal entities > PEO (Professional Employer Organization/ Employer of Record and not a GitLab entity or Branch)

rows.answer: Yes—you can expense a standing desk as part of your home‑office setup. Desks (including work tables) are listed as approved furniture for remote work, and they are covered under the equipment stipend. [2] [4]

rows.q: My company purchasing card was stolen. Who do I tell?
rows.answer: Report the loss immediately to the Accounts Payable Analyst, who will begin the cancellation process. Then, as soon as possible, open a Compass ticket to notify the expense‑admin team so the card can be confirmed cancelled and the account reconciled. [1]
cited: Navan Purchasing Card > 7. PROCEDURES > 7.4 Card Lost or Stolen

rows.q: Can I buy gift cards with the purchasing card?
rows.answer: Gift cards cannot be purchased with the Navan Purchasing Card. All gift‑card requests must be submitted as a Virtual Card request through Zip, and gift cards are excluded from the team‑building benefit because they are taxable for employees【1】. Additionally, the permissible‑gifts policy explicitly states that “Gift cards for team members are not allowed for these gifts”【4】. Therefore, you may not buy gift cards with the purchasing card.

rows.q: How do I kick off the procurement process for a new vendor?
rows.answer:
1. Notify your Procurement Category Manager that you are starting a vendor selection and create an issue with the **RFP Intake template**, tagging the manager. [1]  
2. If the spend is **under $25 k**, submit a **Zip Request** for a purchase request (new spend) in the Zip system. [2]  
3. If the spend is **$25 k – $100 k**, run a business‑led quick‑bid RFP (2 vendor bids). [2]  
4. If the spend is **$100 k – $250 k**, run a business‑led RFP (2‑3 vendor bids). [2]  
5. If the spend is **over $250 k**, run a procurement‑led RFP (5+ vendor bids). [2]  
6. Before any contract or pricing discussion, tell the vendor you will send the agreement to procurement for review. [3]  
7. Obtain a Mutual NDA from the vendor before sharing confidential information. [1]  
8. Ensure the vendor will sign the GitLab Partner Code of Ethics. [1]
cited: The GitLab Procurement Team > What is Procurement? > Vendor Lifecycle Management > 1. RFP and Vendor Selection
The GitLab Procurement Team > The Procurement Process > How to start the Procurement Process
The GitLab Procurement Team > The Procurement Process

rows.q: When does a vendor need a financial viability check?
rows.answer: A vendor requires a financial viability check when any of the following applies: the vendor is a private company, LLC, or self‑employed; the services are needed for continued operations; the services are cloud hosting; the services are directly tied to servicing customers with an uptime requirement; the vendor stores data that cannot be recovered if the vendor goes out of business; or the software or services would take more than one week to replace or swap. [1]
cited: The GitLab Procurement Team > Third Party Risk Management > When do we require a financial viability check?

rows.q: I need something purchased urgently. What should I do?
rows.answer:
Post an escalation in the **#procurement** Slack channel that includes:

- A link to your purchase request (Zip request for general procurement or Coupa request for Field Marketing & Events)  
- The date you need the purchase completed  
- A specific, quantifiable business impact if the date is missed (e.g., “price will increase $45 K if not signed by Friday”) [1][2]

These urgent requests will be evaluated, but note they are disruptive and may be denied if the reason isn’t concrete. To avoid escalation, enter the request into Zip or Coupa **1–2 weeks before the needed date** whenever possible [1][2].
cited: The GitLab Procurement Team > The Procurement Process > What if I have an Urgent Request?
Field Marketing and Events > What if I have an Urgent Request?

rows.q: What are the exceptions to the PO policy?
rows.answer:
The PO Policy does not apply to:

- One‑time purchases under $5 K (or less than $5 K annually)  
- Charitable contributions (donations)  
- Interview‑candidate reimbursement  
- Confidential outside‑counsel legal fees  
- Confidential recruiting engagements  
- Statutory tax fees  
- PEO providers  
- AR/customer refunds  
- Board‑of‑director payments  
- Financing, banking and investing (including interest, debt, FX, fees)  
- Corporate credit‑card expenses  
- Urgent payments not covered above (must be approved by the VP, Corporate Controller and/or PAO)  

[1]
cited: The GitLab Procurement Team > What are the exceptions to the PO Policy?

rows.q: What is Coupa?
rows.answer: Coupa is a cloud‑based purchasing and payment platform that GitLab began using on 2021‑06‑01 for US and Netherlands entities and on 2021‑12‑13 for the remaining entities. It provides an easy‑to‑use interface for suppliers to connect with GitLab, and all new purchase orders, invoices and communications are managed through the Coupa Supplier Portal. [1][2]

rows.q: What is RLOA?
rows.answer: RLOA stands for the **Rolling List of Asks**, a quarterly‑by‑quarter list of key incremental investment requests that business leaders submit to Finance. It is maintained by FBPs together with functional leaders, prioritized, and used by FP&A to develop recommendations, secure funding, and incorporate approved asks into the final forecast and investor guidance. rows.answer: GitLab prefers to engage contingent workers through a third‑party agency rather than as independent contractors, using the agency route whenever possible and reserving independent‑contractor agreements for true consulting relationships only. [1] [3]

rows.q: How do invoice cancellations and refunds work for customers?
rows.answer:
Invoice cancellations and refunds are processed in Stripe and then reflected in Zuora:

1. Log in to Stripe and search for the cardholder’s name. [1]  
2. Open the original charge and click **Refund**. [1]  
3. Enter the refund amount, reason code, and in the description field include the reason and the Zuora invoice number. [1]  
4. Click **Refund**. [1]  
5. Return to Zuora: put the customer account in silent mode under “Communication Profile,” post the invoice draft, and transfer the amount to a credit balance using the accounting code **Stripe – Inc**. [1]  
6. Restore the account to Default/B2B under “Communication Profile.” [1]  
7. Verify the refund invoice shows a $0.00 balance due. [1]  
8. Manually email the customer (do not use Zuora’s email function); attach a screenshot of the Stripe partial refund and a copy of the refund invoice. [1]
cited: Accounting and Reporting > Quote to cash > Invoice cancellations and refunds

rows.q: What is a PID in the hiring plan?
rows.answer: A PID (Position ID) is a unique identifier assigned by the Corporate FP&A team to every approved headcount position in the Hiring Plan. It links approved headcount to the Hiring Plan, increases visibility and accuracy for headcount forecasting (count and dollars), and provides transparency on modeled headcount (attrition and backfill) [5]. All PIDs are created and maintained by FP&A when the Hiring Plan is finalized or when a change request is submitted [2].
cited: Financial Planning & Analysis > Headcount Forecast and Hiring Plan > Hiring Plan Process > Creating a Position ID (PID)
Financial Planning & Analysis > Headcount Forecast and Hiring Plan > Position ID (PID)

rows.q: What is the trading window?
rows.answer: The trading window is the period when insiders are allowed to trade company securities. It opens on the third trading day after the quarterly results are announced and closes immediately before the last four weeks of the fiscal quarter, unless the CLO shortens it because material non‑public information exists. [1]
cited: Investor Relations > Trading Window

rows.q: At what point do I need to use Zip instead of Navan for a purchase?
rows.answer:
You must use Zip (to request a Virtual Card) for any purchase that falls under the non‑permissible items listed:

- Gift‑card purchases – submit the request via Zip. [1]  
- Monthly recurring vendor charges under $5,000 USD – request via Zip. [2]  
- All software subscriptions (e.g., Amazon, Dropbox, Adobe) – submit a Purchase Request through Zip. [3]  
- Prize purchases – request a Virtual Card through Zip (Swag prizes follow the merchandise workflow). [4]  
- Meals for customer/partner dinners – expense them via the Employee reimbursement process **or** request a Virtual Card via Zip. [5]

rows.q: Once an invoice is submitted, how does Finance decide when it gets paid?
rows.answer: Finance looks at the invoice’s due date (or the vendor’s contract payment terms, whichever is earlier) and whether the invoice has been fully approved in ZIP before the Thursday payment cut‑off. If it is approved by Wednesday EOD it will be included in that week’s Thursday run; otherwise it rolls to the next run. “Urgent Payment” requests are placed in the next available run as long as they are fully approved, but AP cannot accommodate same‑day payments. Payments are then released on Thursday and may take 1‑5 business days to reach the vendor’s bank. [1][2]
cited: Accounts Payable > Accounts Payable Payments
Accounts Payable > General Guidelines

rows.q: When does Finance need to record an expense as an accrued liability instead of waiting until it's paid?
rows.answer: Finance must record an expense as an accrued liability when the expense is incurred — i.e., when the product or service has been received on or before the last day of the month being closed—rather than waiting for payment. The liability is recognized at that time because the risk of ownership has passed and the expense has been incurred during the month. [4] The policy also requires that any expense ≥ $5 K be recorded in the period it was incurred, with the accrual process completed monthly/quarterly to ensure accurate liability recording. [2]
cited: Accounting and Reporting > Accounting Policies > Accrued Liabilities Policy
Accounting and Reporting > Accounting Policies > Accrued Liabilities Policy
